description: Prompts for modelling the indicative tax position of selling an Australian investment property — cost base, gross capital gain, 50% CGT discount eligibility, estimated CGT per owner, and net proceeds. Preparation for a registered tax agent, not tax advice.

cards.title: Capital Gains and Net Proceeds Estimate
cards.description: Model the indicative cost base, gross capital gain, CGT per owner, and estimated net proceeds of selling an Australian investment property.
cards.prompt:
You are an Australian capital gains tax preparation analyst. I am thinking about selling an investment property and want an indicative picture of the capital gain, the likely CGT, and my net proceeds — ready to take to a registered tax agent. Every number you give me must be labelled an estimate to verify.

SALE DETAILS:
- Purchase price: $[amount]
- Purchase date: [DD/MM/YYYY] (this sets the > 12-month CGT discount test)
- Sale price: $[amount or indicative estimate] (label unverified if it is not a signed contract)
- Buying costs: $[stamp duty + legal/conveyancing + other acquisition costs]
- Capital improvements: $[cost of capital improvements — cost-base additions, not repairs]
- Selling costs: $[agent commission + marketing + legal/conveyancing on sale]
- Ownership structure + split: [e.g. 50/50 tenants in common / sole owner / company / trust]
- Ever my main residence?: [never / yes — which periods]
- Held > 12 months?: [yes / no]
- Each owner's marginal tax rate: [e.g. Owner A 37%, Owner B 32.5%]
- Loan payout (if known): $[amount, or 'confirm with lender']

Please return a structured estimate with exactly these 6 sections:
1. Cost Base Build-Up (table — each component visible and checkable)
2. Gross Capital Gain (flag if it is a capital loss instead)
3. CGT Discount Eligibility (> 12 months held? individual/trust vs company — companies get no 50% discount)
4. Estimated CGT by Owner (one row per owner, at each owner's marginal rate, + optional 2% Medicare)
5. Net Proceeds After Selling Costs & CGT (before any main-residence exemption)
6. Timing & Questions for Your Tax Agent

Do NOT determine the main-residence exemption or 6-year rule yourself — flag it as verify-with-tax-agent and model the non-exempt case, clearly labelled. Treat only genuine capital improvements as cost-base additions, not repairs — flag anything ambiguous.

DISCLAIMER: NOT TAX ADVICE. General information and educational preparation only. Every figure is an estimate, not a tax calculation you can rely on. CGT law and rates change — verify current rules with the ATO and a registered tax agent before acting.
cards.best_for: Investors weighing up whether to sell an investment property who want an indicative CGT and net-proceeds picture before speaking with their registered tax agent
cards.output_type: 6-section CGT estimate including cost-base build-up, gross gain, discount eligibility, CGT-by-owner table, net proceeds, and questions for the tax agent
cards.professional_review_note: NOT TAX ADVICE. Every figure is an estimate. Take this to a registered tax agent to confirm the main-residence exemption, cost-base treatment, timing, and any carried-forward losses. CGT law and rates change — verify current rules with the ATO.

cards.title: Sale Timing and Main-Residence Exemption Questions
cards.description: Surface the timing and main-residence exemption questions to take to a registered tax agent before committing to a sale — without computing the exemption.
cards.prompt:
You are an Australian capital gains tax preparation analyst. I am planning to sell an investment property and want to understand the timing levers and main-residence exemption questions I should raise with my registered tax agent before I commit. Do NOT compute the main-residence exemption or 6-year rule for me — I understand only a registered tax agent can determine that.

MY SITUATION:
- Purchase date: [DD/MM/YYYY]
- Expected sale/contract timing: [approx date, or 'flexible']
- Held > 12 months by expected contract date?: [yes / no / borderline]
- Ever my main residence?: [never / yes — which periods, and did I rent it out after moving out?]
- Ownership structure: [sole owner / tenants in common split / company / trust]
- Any carried-forward capital losses?: [yes / no / unsure]

Please return:
1. Timing considerations — how the contract date (not settlement) affects which financial year the gain is taxed in, whether selling before/after 30 June matters, and whether holding just past the 12-month mark changes 50% discount eligibility (framed as questions, not advice)
2. Main-residence exemption questions to ask my tax agent (including the 6-year rule) — flag these as things only the tax agent can determine
3. Cost base questions — which improvement costs count vs which were already deducted as repairs
4. Ownership-structure questions — how my structure changes the CGT outcome
5. Loss and offset questions — carried-forward capital losses

IMPORTANT: Note that CGT law, rates, and thresholds change. Do not present any exemption or timing outcome as settled — everything is a question to verify with a registered tax agent and the ATO.

DISCLAIMER: NOT TAX ADVICE. General information and educational preparation only. This does not determine the main-residence exemption, the 6-year rule, or any other concession — only a registered tax agent can.
cards.best_for: Investors who want to get the timing and main-residence exemption questions right before speaking with their registered tax agent, without an AI attempting to determine the exemption
cards.output_type: Structured list of timing considerations and tax-agent questions covering the main-residence exemption, cost base, ownership structure, and carried-forward losses
cards.professional_review_note: NOT TAX ADVICE. The main-residence exemption and 6-year rule can only be determined by a registered tax agent. Use this to prepare questions, not to reach conclusions. Verify current CGT rules with the ATO.
